rubrics.justification: The response gives a largely accurate blastocyst description consistent with an AB-quality embryo, including reasonable comments on ICM compactness, TE looseness, and lack of hatching. It appropriately notes the Gardner stage/description inconsistency, though some image-specific details are somewhat inferential from a static view.

It thoroughly integrates age, BMI, FSH, diagnosis, cycle response, sperm parameters, and especially the very thin endometrium, clearly explaining how these factors modify prognosis relative to embryo quality.

The reasoning is structured and internally consistent, with prognosis logically adjusted downward because of the 4.0 mm lining. Minor uncertainty comes from broad probability ranges and some reliance on assumptions about timing of the endometrial measurement.

Recommendations are generally consistent with IVF practice: single embryo transfer in a young patient, caution with thin endometrium, and no routine PGT-A requirement at age 28. Small deviations include somewhat assertive freeze-all language despite limited context on exact timing and pattern of the lining.

The response provides clear next steps for both pre- and post-transfer scenarios, including confirming lining timing, considering freeze-all, uterine cavity evaluation, endometrial optimization strategies, and future cycle planning.
